evidence: The current draft page lists the forward-map, target-class, identifiability, and modulus definitions. The IP-14 Definition uses the metric forward-map and target interface; the restricted B example uses the exact uniform-modulus conditions. The page's kernel theorem is not used. This is an interface check only, not independent approval.

The actual Definition supplies metric parameter/data spaces, a nonempty admissible truth class, a forward map, and a metric target map. The new Definition adopts those interfaces and adds a measurable additive-noise sampling law. This verifies the declared interface only; it is not approval.

The actual Definition requires a nondecreasing modulus omega with omega(0)=0, limit zero at the origin, and target distance bounded by data distance for every admissible pair. The example checks every pair in its restricted configuration class against this exact interface. This is an interface check only; it is not approval.

The actual page and both item bodies were inspected. The isonormal definition provides the functional white-noise model and the theorem supplies its fixed-basis coordinate representation. IP-14 retains the page prerequisite, but no IP-14 item assumes a Gaussian or white-noise law; the equal-law example works for any common additive noise law. This is a page-interface check only, not approval.

The actual page and its four A-item bodies were inspected, including the complete exact-risk proof. That model's Countable Choice assumption is inherited from the compact-SVD coordinate construction. IP-14 uses none of its sequence estimators or risk identities, and imports no choice axiom; the declared page edge remains context only. This is a page-interface check only, not approval.

The current published page contains the loss/risk definition used for the extended metric risk, including its measurable action-kernel integrand, and the separately inspected action-law measurability lemma. This records the extra task and plan-spec edge retained despite the track-plan discrepancy; it is a supplier-interface check, not approval.
